response:
Diagnosis after gen-6. Three results reshape the search. (i) The winsorization test returned *identical* statistics to the raw ratio, which means the evaluation already trims tails — so the net-hidden-capital signal's fmb of 0.71 is not a skew artifact but tells us that a price-scaled hidden-capital level has no linear cross-sectional slope; only ranked legs carry FMB information here. (ii) Discrete accounting states keep working: "unrecorded capital exceeds recorded equity" delivered fmb 4.96 with Sharpe 0.483, and the net-creditor state still holds the alpha record (7.7%). (iii) The MAX union (5.2%) underperformed the SUMRANK average (6.1%) with the same legs, and the retreat penalty destroyed alpha (0.6%), so subtractive penalties and set-union aggregation are both dead ends. With two generations left after this, I concentrate on the discrete-state family (which uniquely gives both fmb and alpha), one anchor-level consolidation of the two best components, and two capital-formation mechanisms that unify channels instead of stacking them.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Brand-and-Knowledge Cheapness in Net-Creditor Firms
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5))), INDICATOR(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), 0)))
HYPOTHESIS: The cross-sectional slope and the portfolio alpha in this archive are carried by two different components — the breadth of the organic-capital conditioner and the solvency state — and combining the best version of each should deliver joint strength rather than an intermediate blend.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive's fmb leader among two-leg composites is the brand-and-knowledge share (fmb 5.01, Sharpe 0.596, alpha 6.4%) and its alpha leader is the net-creditor state (alpha 7.7%, t 5.12, fmb 2.87), and because the solvency leg is a scale-free binary it cannot mechanically dilute the conditioner's slope the way an asset-scaled continuous leg does. This is the one consolidation whose outcome is diagnostic: an intermediate result would confirm a genuine fmb/alpha frontier, while joint improvement would identify the final signal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Cheapness in Doubly Favorable Accounting States
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MUL(INDICATOR(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 0), INDICATOR(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), 0)))
HYPOTHESIS: The mispricing is concentrated in firms that simultaneously satisfy two discrete conditions — more capital built off the balance sheet than on it, and liquid assets exceeding all debt — because the first makes reported value meaningless and the second guarantees the hidden capital will not be liquidated in distress.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Both states have been evaluated separately and each is strong on a different metric (unrecorded-exceeds-recorded: fmb 4.96, Sharpe 0.483; net creditor: alpha 7.7%), and their product is a conjunction rather than a rank average, so it identifies a specific population rather than averaging two orderings. The construction is scale-free, immune to the 1/P duplication problem, and produces a stable, well-populated flagged group instead of a distressed tail.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Cheap Innovators with Expanding Gross Margin
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: Knowledge capital shows up first in pricing power, so the cleanest evidence that a firm's intangible investment is converting is a widening gross margin — a bounded, unit-free quantity — rather than growth in the dollar level of gross profit or in gross profit per asset.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The conversion channel is the only profitability-related conditioner that has ever added alpha here (6.8% with GROWTH of gross profit, 4.6% with the assets-scaled change), and the two implementations differ precisely in whether the denominator moves with asset accumulation; a margin definition removes that confound and keeps coverage near 0.13. It also separates conversion from scale expansion, which matters because asset growth is priced by CMA and was plausibly eroding the assets-scaled version.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Cheap Firms Investing in Knowledge Not Assets
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(GROWTH(at, 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms substituting intangible for tangible investment expand economic capital while their balance sheet stands still; cheap firms in this asset-light configuration accumulate value that neither book equity nor asset-growth-based factors capture.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a capital-formation composition mechanism the archive has not tested — every previous conditioner measured intangible intensity in levels, never against the firm's contemporaneous tangible investment — and the differenced-rank form means a firm scores highly only if it is building knowledge *instead of* assets, not merely doing both. The two ranks are bounded and full-coverage, and the asset-growth component is the part FF5 already prices, so any incremental alpha must come from the intangible side of the substitution.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Cheapness Graded by Accounting Conservatism
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUB(INDICATOR(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 0), INDICATOR(SUB(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 0)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms fall into three accounting regimes — conservative, where unrecorded knowledge capital exceeds recorded equity; aggressive, where goodwill from acquisitions exceeds the remaining hard equity; and neutral — and cheapness is informative in the first regime, meaningless in the second, and ordinary in the third.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The discrete-state family is the only genuinely new mechanism this archive has found that scores well on fmb, but every version so far has been one-sided; a signed three-level state adds the short side explicitly, which is where the archive's long-short spreads have been weakest. Both indicators compare balance-sheet quantities to each other with no price or asset scaling, so the state cannot be triggered by a price collapse and cannot duplicate the value anchor.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Self-Built and Unlevered Versus Bought and Borrowed
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(dltt, dlc)), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: How a firm acquired its capital and how it paid for it are one economic decision: capital built internally and funded from operations is unrecorded and unencumbered, while capital bought with debt is both capitalised at deal price and pledged against creditors, so the contrast between the two is the sharpest description of a cheap firm's hidden value.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Rather than stacking the builders-versus-buyers conditioner (5.4% alpha) and the leverage conditioner (6.5% alpha) as separate ranks, this fuses them into a single capital-formation-and-financing composition variable, which is the unified form the two channels' shared collateral logic implies. Both components are asset-scaled ranks defined for the whole cross-section, so coverage stays at ~0.14, and the comparison against both parents will show whether the unification adds information or merely reproduces their average.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Brand-and-Knowledge Cheapness in Net-Creditor Firms---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is the archive's already-evaluated "Cheap Innovators That Are Net Creditors" with the R&D share swapped for the equally already-evaluated xrd+xad share — a cosmetic two-leg recombination explicitly motivated by picking the fmb-leader and alpha-leader rather than by any new economics.

---CRITIQUE Cheapness in Doubly Favorable Accounting States---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The conjunction of two indicators is a marginally different construction than a rank average, but both states are already in the archive and the resulting conditioner is a coarse 0/1/2 variable whose flagged population (R&D stock above hard book *and* net cash) is likely dominated by small, cash-rich micro-innovators, so it mostly re-slices existing evidence.

---CRITIQUE Cheap Innovators with Expanding Gross Margin---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is the third implementation of the same "conversion" conditioner (after GROWTH of gross profit and DELTA of gross profit/assets), differing only in the scaling denominator, which is exactly the kind of cosmetic variant the objective warns against.

---CRITIQUE Cheap Firms Investing in Knowledge Not Assets---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The intangible-versus-tangible investment substitution conditioner is a genuinely new construction for this archive and internally consistent, but its short-side driver is essentially the canonical asset-growth anomaly (already partly spanned by CMA), so incremental alpha over the existing builders-versus-buyers and non-dilution variants is uncertain, and the claim that "any incremental alpha must come from the intangible side" is not established.

---CRITIQUE Cheapness Graded by Accounting Conservatism---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The signed goodwill-heavy short state is a worthwhile new addition, but the stated hypothesis (cheapness "informative in one regime, meaningless in another") requires an interaction while the expression merely adds a ternary state to the B/M rank, so the construction does not implement the mechanism claimed.

---CRITIQUE Self-Built and Unlevered Versus Bought and Borrowed---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Summing goodwill and total debt into one asset-scaled term is an arbitrary fusion of two already-tested conditioners with no clear reason the two should carry equal weight, and the proposal itself concedes the likely outcome is the average of its parents.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Cheapness with a Long Innovation Runway
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), WINSOR(RATIO(che, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(dltt, dlc))), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: The relevant liquidity measure for an innovator is not cash relative to assets but cash relative to its annual claims — the research program it must keep funding plus the debt it must service; firms with many years of runway can carry knowledge capital to maturity, and when they are also cheap the market is pricing a survival risk that does not exist.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: Unlike the archive's financing legs, which are pure balance-sheet ratios bolted alongside an intangible conditioner, this quantity is itself a cross-theme construct — the intangible commitment sits in the denominator of the liquidity measure — so the two themes interact inside a single variable rather than being averaged. The denominator is a sum of non-negative claims and WINSOR controls the tail for firms with tiny claims, while coverage remains near the incumbent family since almost every firm has some debt or some R&D.
REASONING_END: n/a

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Cheap Firms Crossing Into Accounting Opacity
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), DELTA(INDICATOR(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 0), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: The year a firm's accumulated unrecorded capital first exceeds its recorded equity is the moment conventional value metrics stop describing it; screens, index rules and analyst models update slowly, so cheap firms at that crossing are freshly and temporarily misclassified.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This converts a static regime indicator into an event: the transition itself, which identifies newly misclassified firms rather than the long-standing population of research-intensive small caps that the level indicator selects. It is a timing mechanism rather than a re-slice of existing states, the flagged group refreshes every year so decile composition is not a persistent micro-cap bet, and coverage is unchanged because the differenced indicator is defined for all firms.
REASONING_END: n/a

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Cheapness with Overstated Reported Leverage
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), ADD(ceq, ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), ADD(ADD(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), ADD(dltt, dlc))))))
HYPOTHESIS: Because expensing shrinks book equity, reported debt-to-capital overstates the true leverage of intangible-intensive firms; the wedge between reported and economically restated leverage measures how much a firm's risk is exaggerated by accounting, and cheap firms with a large wedge are discounted for a risk they do not bear.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This explains, rather than repeats, why the archive's leverage and solvency legs added alpha: the channel is risk *misclassification* caused by the same understatement that drives the value effect, and the wedge isolates it while the raw leverage level does not. Both legs are bounded ranks with strictly positive denominators, the wedge is exactly zero for firms with no R&D and no goodwill so they sit neutrally in the middle, and coverage stays at roughly 0.14.
REASONING_END: n/a

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Cheapness Gated by Accounting Regime
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), SUB(INDICATOR(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 0), INDICATOR(SUB(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), 0)))
HYPOTHESIS: Book-based cheapness means opposite things in opposite accounting regimes: for conservatively accounted firms a low price relative to hard book understates value, while for goodwill-dominated firms the same ratio reflects a book that is itself inflated deal residue, so those cheap firms are traps.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This now implements the interaction the previous version only claimed — the cheapness rank is signed by the regime, so the long leg is cheap-and-conservative and the short leg is cheap-and-goodwill-heavy, exactly the two populations the hypothesis distinguishes. It differs from the failed gen-0 multiplicative signal, which shrank a signed value score by a positive intensity rank and therefore scrambled the extremes; here the positive rank is multiplied by a signed state, which orders the cross-section coherently and puts economically distinct firms at each end.
REASONING_END: n/a

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Cheapness with Restated Economic Return on Capital
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Profitability is only informative for intangible-intensive firms when earnings and capital are restated consistently — R&D added back to income and capitalised into the capital base — and cheap firms whose restated return on economic capital is high are genuinely profitable businesses that reported accounting merely disguises.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The archive's failed profitability conditioners were internally inconsistent: gross profit (unrestated numerator) divided by an intangible-inclusive capital base, which mechanically penalises research-intensive firms and is spanned by RMW. Restating both sides is a different quantity that is largest exactly where the accounting distortion is largest, so it should not be absorbed by the reported-operating-profitability factor, and WINSOR plus the hard-book-plus-stock denominator controls the small-capital tail.
REASONING_END: n/a
